item.title: Wild Parakeets nuisance to residents, 23rd August
item.description:
Thank you for your response regarding the ring-necked parakeet population in Orpington. ​While I understand the Council’s position regarding wide-spread culling on public land and national Biodiversity Action Plans, my primary concern centers on the immediate local impact—specifically severe, concentrated noise nuisance, loss of quiet enjoyment, and potential risk of localized tree and structural damage in residential areas. ​Although a wide-spread cull may not be under consideration, local authorities retain a responsibility to manage public land where non-native species generate a localized public nuisance or impact environmental quality. I would appreciate clarification on the following points: ​Statutory Nuisance & Public Health: Does the Council monitor or assess localized roosting sites when noise levels significantly impact residents' wellbeing and sleep, independent of wider biodiversity metrics? ​Non-Lethal Management: Given that culling is ruled out, what non-lethal mitigation measures (such as acoustic deterrents, canopy pruning at identified roosting hotspots, or roost dispersal techniques) is the Council willing to deploy to manage flock concentration near residential properties? ​Property & Infrastructure Monitoring: Ring-necked parakeets are recognized by Natural England as capable of causing localized structural and tree damage. Has the Council conducted any localized risk assessments on mature public trees near housing in Orpington to inspect for canopy damage or nesting wear? ​Rather than requesting a wide-scale population reduction, I am asking the Council to proactively manage specific, high-density roosting spots on public land to mitigate the impact on nearby homes. ​I look forward to a resolution.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): High Street, Ramsden, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: Pavement bollard position making access to my driveway very difficult, 23rd August
item.description:
A pavement bollard positioned very close to my driveway way is making access to my driveway very difficult. I have nearly collided with it many times and I would like it to be removed as it is an accident waiting to happen. Over the years my road has become more congested, many more cars parked on the street, particularly during school pick up and drop off times and it is becoming increasingly difficult to manoeuvre my car into my driveway, given the position of the bollard. My road is also very narrow which makes the angle needed to swing my car in place, whilst avoiding the bollard extremely tricky. I have nearly hit the bollard numerous times. I would like the council to remove the bollard before I (or visitors) to my house hit the bollard and damaged it and their car. The bollard serves no useful purpose as far as I can ascertain.
